transcript: I only saw midnight this week and I have so many thoughts. I have to acknowledge the fact that midnight is my entire FYP right now. It is not my place to tell anyone how to feel about the show. Wanna keep this mostly spoiler free, but I do think there is a responsibility to let people know what they're walking into. Set in the American South during the time that black people were enslaved, it depicts enslaved people being subjected to horrific abuse and violence by their enslavers. You're welcome to DM me if you have any specific questions about what's being depicted. I also want to acknowledge that I am a white woman. My experience of watching a story about the enslavement of black people is fundamentally different from that of a black audience member. I cannot speak to that experience, and my thoughts on the show do not invalidate anyone else's. I was invited by press to share my thoughts on the show, and so I want to share them with you. Midnight is an epic in every sense of the word. We're in the Darwin Theatre, which is a small theatre, but this show is massive scale. The music, the storytelling, the ambition. Follows 12 principal characters. A lot of character at its center is rail, who is played by Todrick Hall. Rail was born into enslavement, was ripped from his family as a baby. But the majority of the story is around his connection with His white neighbor Richard, who hires and pays rail to help him build his house for him and his fiance. Richard is trying to build an integrated house, one that would employ both black and white people. I'm very clear here, cause I've seen a lot of misinformation. Rail is. Is enslaved, though, by Richard's fiance's family. There's a little bit of a Cinderella story woven in here. There's a prince, there's evil stepsisters, there's glass and a shoe separate. And of course, midnight. But it's very much an original story and original musical. It's honestly one of the most beautifully visual shows I've ever seen. Staging, the lighting, the costumes, the choreography. Outside of the 12 principles, there's also an ensemble, and these folks dance. And the performances this entire cast is giving are unreal. It's entirely sung through. The score pulls from gospel and pop and R&B, and the sheer vocal talent is just un match. I think it's perfect. No, but that's the point of a run like this, is to workshop all the things that are working and are not working. Storylines that can be tightened. There are characters that I think could be almost entirely rewritten. The big twist that happens at the end of the first act that I think needs to be clearer. This is a massive swing. Even when every single element doesn't land for me, was fully engaged in what this entire cast was doing. Roger Callas created something that is Visually stunning, Musically exhilarating, and very, very emotionally complicated. Obviously, I think there is a lot of room for conversations and criticism. Walked out of midnight feeling like I had seen something that was truly unique and wildly ambitious and completely original. And I feel like that is what I've asked for from new theater for a long time. A lot more thoughts, a lot more things I could say. I'll leave it here for now. Tonight is playing at the Daryl Rae Theater through November 8th. I am so curious to see where it goes from here.
